blocks.text: Everything written outside a volume goes to the container's writable layer (overlay2 upperdir), which is deleted when the container is removed, including every recreate and every deploy of a new image.

$ docker diff api          # A=added, C=changed, D=deleted
A /app/uploads/report.pdf  # state that should be on a volume
$ docker ps -s             # writable-layer size per container

items: Copy-up and overlay overhead make write-heavy workloads slow.

blocks.text: Images like postgres declare `VOLUME`; without a mount, Docker creates an anonymous volume. A new container gets a new empty one and the old one is orphaned, so always mount a named volume explicitly.

Q: "Where does data written inside a container go, and when is it lost?" A: "Into the container's writable layer, which survives stop and restart but is deleted with the container, so any recreate or new-image deploy loses it. Durable state must go to a volume or an external service."

items: Writable layer lives and dies with the container.
